approved: Sex Discrimination Amendment (Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Intersex Status) Bill 2013

The majority voted in favour of government [amendments (1)-(3)](http://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22legislation%2Famend%2Fr5026_amend_09ede765-843c-4069-8241-e22cb2bb84bb%22).(Read the discussion leading up to the division [here](http://www.openaustralia.org/senate/?id=2013-06-24.155.1). ) This means that they were successful. The amendments relate to Commonwealth funded aged care and exclude this type of aged care from the exemption in the bill that allows religious organisations to discriminate on religious grounds. In other words, the amendments mean that religious organisations that provide Commonwealth funded age care cannot refuse to provide homosexual older people with their services. The purpose of the amendments is to ensure "the ability of older people to access aged care services without discrimination".(Read more about these amendments in their [explanatory memorandum](http://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22legislation%2Fems%2Fr5026_ems_3afab29a-1766-4409-baac-5c1217ee6adf%22). ) Liberal Senator [Sue Boyce](http://publicwhip-rails.openaustraliafoundation.org.au/mp.php?mpn=Sue_Boyce&mpc=Senate&house=senate) rebelled in this division by crossing the floor and voting 'aye' with the Government.(Read more about what it means to rebel in our [FAQ section](http://publicwhip-rails.openaustraliafoundation.org.au/faq.php#rebelandfree). ) _Background to the bill_ This [bill](http://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r5026) provides new protections against discrimination on the basis of a person’s [sexual orientation](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_orientation), [gender identity](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_identity) and [intersex status](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intersex).(Read more about the bill in its [bills digest](http://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/download/legislation/billsdgs/2536109/upload_binary/2536109.pdf;f

Confirmed coalition support for the Sex Discrimination Amendment (Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Intersex Status) Bill 2013, noting it adopts a policy the coalition took to the 2010 election, and flagged possible Senate amendments following the government's earlier abandonment of its Human Rights and Anti-Discrimination Bill on 20 March.

Championed the Sex Discrimination Amendment Bill 2013 as extending overdue protections against discrimination on sexual orientation, gender identity and intersex status, building on earlier reforms to 85 Commonwealth acts removing discrimination against same-sex couples, and thanked the opposition for its bipartisan support.
